description: Docker + GitHub Actions hardening. Group base images, group common actions, flag runtime majors as breaking, track version-pinned global npm installs in Dockerfiles.

packageRules.description: Dockerfile base images — group bumps + digest pins together. EXCLUDES the language-runtime images, which are toolchain moves rather than base-image moves and must ride in their own runtime group so an interpreter and the manifest that pins it never bump separately: node/pnpm -> node.json's `toolchain-versions` (`.nvmrc`, `engines.node`, `packageManager`); python -> python.json's `python runtime` (an exact `requires-python = "==X.Y.Z"` pin). Consumers extend `:node`/`:python` BEFORE `:docker`, so without this carve-out the later preset's groupName wins (last matching rule wins) and each runtime splits across two PRs that CANNOT go green independently — owine/doc-scanner #145/#146 (ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE on both halves) and owine/trip-tracker #180/#182 (`No interpreter found for Python 3.14.6` on one side, `not compatible with the locked Python requirement` on the other). Deliberately NOT solved by preset ordering: `extends` order lives in each consumer's renovate.json, and no consumer should have to know that grouping depends on it. Negatives-only list on purpose — Renovate rejects mixing `*` with `!` (see docs/string-pattern-matching), and an all-negative array matches everything not listed. Entries are plain strings, which are glob-matched with `.` and `/` literal, so they are exact matches: `python-slim`, `my.registry/python`, and `docker.io/library/postgres` all still group here. The names mirror the runtime rules in node.json/python.json EXACTLY; keep them in sync, or an excluded dep lands in no group at all and deadlocks the same way. This does NOT affect digest pinning: `pinDigests` comes from default.json's `matchManagers: [dockerfile, github-actions]` rule, which is untouched — the runtime images' digest/pinDigest updates simply group under their runtime name instead of `dockerfile bases`. `pinDigest` IS NO LONGER IN THIS RULE'S matchUpdateTypes, and that is load-bearing rather than tidying: default.json schedules `pin`/`pinDigest` `at any time` and automerge.json gives them their own `pins` branch, but this preset is extended AFTER both, so listing `pinDigest` here won the groupName and parked every tag->digest conversion back on this weekly branch — silently undoing the override, since a branch gets ONE schedule. A base image's FIRST digest pin now rides `pins` and lands immediately; every subsequent digest REFRESH still rides this group, which is the correct split, because a refresh re-points an unchanged tag at different bytes (a content change) while the conversion changes nothing at all.

GitHub Actions setup family — the checkout + toolchain steps that open almost every job. Grouped for the order-coupling that reviewing either action alone would hide: `actions/setup-node` with `cache: pnpm` only works if `pnpm/setup` ran first, so a major on either side needs the other in the same diff. Since the pnpm/setup v3 migration that coupling survives in exactly two jobs fleet-wide — the `publish` jobs in unifi-network-mcp and unifi-protect-mcp, where setup-node stays for registry auth and the npm binary. Everywhere else `pnpm/setup` alone now provides pnpm, Node, the store cache and the install, so setup-node is not in the job at all and the two move independently; the group is free there and load-bearing only in those two publish jobs. Names `pnpm/setup`, NOT its predecessor `pnpm/action-setup` — action-setup is pnpm v10-and-older only and the fleet is on pnpm 11+, so a compatibility entry would just be a second name to go stale. NOTE: this is an allowlist, so a renamed or newly-adopted action silently drops out of the group (it stays digest-pinned and automerged — those rules key off matchManagers — but loses its grouping); re-audit against real workflow usage when adding toolchains.
GitHub Actions artifact family — upload + download must stay paired
Runtime/data-tier major bumps are breaking-change candidates — extra labels

customManagers.description: Bump version-pinned global npm installs in Dockerfiles: a `# renovate: datasource=X depName=Y` hint comment immediately followed by `RUN npm install -g pkg@VERSION`. Renovate's native dockerfile manager only sees FROM lines, so this reaches global tool installs (serve, pnpm, etc.). INVARIANT: inter-field separators use `[ \t]`, never `\s` — `\s` matches `\n` and cross-attributes fields across blocks (same hazard as the workflow custom manager in default.json).

Track Dockerfile `ARG PNPM_VERSION=…` against the npm `pnpm` package so corepack stays in lockstep with `package.json:packageManager`. Without this, Renovate bumps the npm side, the Dockerfile drifts, and pnpm ≥11 hits ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY when corepack tries a runtime install. Intentionally narrow: only the `ARG PNPM_VERSION=<value>` shape — `ENV …`, `RUN npm i -g pnpm@…`, and bare `corepack prepare pnpm@… --activate` are handled by the customManager above or fall outside scope. Folds into the `toolchain-versions` group in node.json via depName.
Track Dockerfile `ARG YARN_VERSION=…` against the npm `yarn` package. Same corepack drift hazard as pnpm; symmetric solution.
